basis: Defined by degeneration of CNS myelin; immune causation is subtype-dependent.
Immune-mediated inflammation of the limbic brain; the associated cancer is a separate disease.
Cutaneous leiomyomas occur in 80-99%; uterine lesions have no axis. Renal carcinoma is a separately diagnosed cancer predisposition, not universal renal damage.
Progressive nephropathy and hypertension jointly define the disorder.
Inherited infantile liver failure; extrahepatic manifestations depend on subtype.
Definition specifies testicular germ-cell cancers; reproductive tumour origin has no axis and does not establish endocrine disease.
Pontocerebellar hypoplasia and developmental impairment define disease; dysphagia and respiratory insufficiency do not establish direct gastrointestinal or pulmonary injury.
Mandibular agenesis, brain malformations and synotia define disease; severe ocular malformations occur in 80-99%. Cap omits frequent nasal/airway and oral malformations.
Nephrotic renal failure and severe neurodevelopmental disease define syndrome; scoliosis occurs in 1/3 reported patients, meeting the threshold in a small cohort.
Inherited serine-family amino acid metabolic disorders; neurologic injury is prominent in several subtypes but its frequency across the entire umbrella is uncertain.
Autoimmune inflammation damages liver; arthralgia is a symptom, while renal inflammation and arthritis are reported in fewer than 30%.
Carcinoma originates in liver or intrahepatic bile ducts; metastatic potential alone does not establish another affected organ.
Aicardi-Goutieres inflammatory encephalopathy is a type I interferonopathy; skin involvement is not established at >=30% for this specific dominant subtype.
Defective neutrophil function is both a blood-cell disorder and an innate immune deficiency; other organ manifestations vary by subtype.
Hypertrichosis affects hair follicles of the eyelid, combining a hair disorder with a defined ocular-adnexal location.
Benign smooth-muscle tumour grows within and occupies veins; visceral smooth muscle is outside the musculoskeletal axis.
DOK7-related neuromuscular transmission failure causes fetal akinesia and contractures; pulmonary hypoplasia is a major feature of fetal akinesia deformation sequence.
Acetylcholinesterase inhibition causes central, autonomic and neuromuscular dysfunction; transient secretions and bronchospasm do not establish lasting lung damage.
Skin, hair, sweat-gland and dental defects define disease; keratoconjunctivitis sicca occurs in 30-79%. Immunodeficiency is restricted to a rare subtype; asthma is separate.
The umbrella predominantly comprises skeletal-muscle protein disorders and muscular dystrophies; nerve, neuromuscular-junction and cardiac involvement depend on subtype.
Neurodegeneration and optic atrophy define disease; generalized muscle atrophy occurs in 4/4. Respiratory findings in one patient do not establish common direct lung injury.
Site-unspecified polyp umbrella; gastrointestinal mucosal polyps are the predominant clinical group. Other organ locations require a site-specific subtype.
Intestinal lymph leakage causes enteropathy and combined immunodeficiency (80-99%); direct lymphocyte loss produces lymphopenia (30-79%), with anemia reported in 80-99%.
Aplasia cutis and terminal limb-reduction defects define Adams-Oliver syndrome; cardiac and neurologic abnormalities are not established as common in ARHGAP31-related disease.
Limb defects, congenital heart disease and intellectual disability define syndrome; cleft lip/palate occurs in 30-79%. Cap omits urethral hypospadias, also reported in 30-79%.
